# Held-out cases

The agent never reads this folder: no tool can open it, and only `scripts/run_eval.py --split heldout` loads it.

## `heldout_v2.jsonl`: 24 cases

| Type | Cases |
|---|---|
| Numeric | 10 |
| Comparison | 6 |
| Risk change | 4 |
| Refusal | 4 |

**How they were made.** Nobody chose the questions by hand. The set is generated by a fixed rule ([scripts/make_heldout_cases.py](../../../scripts/make_heldout_cases.py)), so it cannot be tuned to the agent:

- every question comes from fixed templates over the 15 covered companies and FY2022–FY2024;
- anything a development case uses is excluded (including the earlier set v1, now in `../dev_extra/`): the same figure, the same company pair, the same risk-change company and years, the same refusal question;
- cases are drawn with a fixed seed (`20261111`), stratified by type, and by sector for numeric cases;
- expected figures are computed from XBRL by code;
- the file and its SHA-256 ([manifest.json](manifest.json)) were committed **before any agent ran on it**.

If the agent is changed after viewing held-out results, the affected cases count as development cases from then on, and the report says so.

**Run** (frozen playbook required unless lessons are off):

```
python scripts/run_eval.py --experiment e1_c0_c1_c2 --tag e1-heldout-v2-run1
```

Then run it again with the tags `-run2` and `-run3`.

More cases can be added as further `*.jsonl` files in this folder, in the same format as `../dev_cases.jsonl`.
